full_judgment:
Shah Abu Nayeem Mominur Rahman J: Instant petition for leave to appeal under Article 103 of the Constitution is against the judgment and order dated 05.10.2009 passed by the High Court Division in discharging the Rule issued in Civil Revision No.2245 of 2007 upholding the judgment and decree dated 08.03.2007 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 6th Court, Dhaka, dismissing the Title Appeal No.122 of 2004 which arose against the judgment and decree dated 31.03,2004 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 5th Court, Dhaka, dismissing the Title Suit No.134 of 2000 filed by the petitioner hereof as plaintiff praying for a decree for Specific Performance of Contract. 

 6. The learned Advocate appearing for the leave petitioner submitted that the courts below erred in law in not noticing that in a case for Specific Performance of Contract only issue to be adjudicated upon is whether the disputed agreement for sale is genuine or not and that the Court acted beyond jurisdiction in considering the nature and propriety of the suit property and authority of the attorney holder to execute the agreement for sale and that heirs of Safiuddin Bhuiyan, the attorney, as well as the attorney himself having had filed the written statement admitting the execution of the agreement for sale of the suit land with the plaintiff, the Court has acted illegally in not decreeing the suit and that the legal heirs of the attorney holder as well as attorney himself, since have admitted the execution and registration of the power of attorney by Ahmed Newaz Bhuiyan in favour of Safiuddin -Bhuiyan as attorney, the Court acted illegally in disbelieving the genuineness of the execution and registration of the power of attorney in reference and that the required permission from the Government can be taken subsequent to the execution and registration of the sale deed by the parties to the sale inasmuch as the Government on receipt of the consideration money has leased out the suit property in favour of the mother of Ahmed Newaz Bhuiyan and also delivered possession to her and thereby Government respondent would not suffer anyway. 

 8. The submissions of the learned Advocate that in a case for Specific Performance of Contract, without considering the nature and character of the suit property, a decree can be passed only on the basis of the document, are not proper and correct inasmuch as no agreement for sale can be made in respect of any land whereupon the seller has no lawful authority to transfer and such document if made, is illegal and can not be enforced in any court of law.
